input.question: What happens if you freeze a super strong container full of water?
input.ground_truth: There are different types of “ice” depending on pressure. Typical ice is ice-I; when freezing water under sufficient pressure, different types all the way to ice-XVI have been produced, some are unstable and can’t be found in nature. Most of these are more dense than water (ie the water would shrink rather than expand). It is hypothesized that under sufficient pressure (e.g. a strong enough container shrinking in size) water would freeze into a metallic form of ice.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: What happens if you freeze a super strong container full of water?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine you have a really, really tough bottle, like a metal one that’s super strong. If you put water inside and put it in the freezer, the water inside will get very, very cold. When water gets very cold, it turns into ice! But because your bottle is super strong, it won’t break when the water turns into ice and gets bigger. So, after a while, you’ll have a strong bottle with a big ice cube inside! 

But if you use a regular bottle that’s not strong, it might break because the ice gets bigger and needs more space. But your super strong bottle will be okay!
